properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-22: "I want CI checks on the 288 capabilities of reflow2… before going any further development we need to get control of testing", after his brother's reaction that this "sounds like it is an AI coding project".

THIS IS THE FIRST QUESTION AND THE OTHER THREE DEPEND ON IT. Measured the same day: 312 Verifications, 311 reading `passing`, 282 with NO EXECUTABLE FORM, 46 never run. Put a Verification on each of the remaining 47 capabilities tomorrow and the design reports 288 of 288 verified — while the number of things a machine can actually re-run stays at about 30. That is the failure mode the critique names, reached by doing exactly what was asked.

⭐ THE VOCABULARY IS ALREADY THERE. `cap:record-to-record-relations-are-modelled` and `req:a-record-can-say-what-runs-it-what-complements-it-and-what-replaced-it` let a Verification NAME THE FILE THAT RUNS IT. Thirty of 312 do. Nothing requires it and nothing reports its absence in a way that changes behaviour — the three-legs shape again, missing the leg that notices.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.

(a) EXECUTABLE FORM IS THE BAR. A Verification counts toward "verified" only if it names a runnable command that EXISTS, and a report distinguishes `verified` from `claimed`. Nothing is deleted; the counts simply stop conflating the two, and 241/288 becomes something like 30/288 overnight. ⚠️ Counter, and it is the real cost: every rollup, the delivery line and the maturity bands all drop hard, and a number that falls by 85% invites being explained away rather than fixed. ⭐ But that IS the honest number, and the current one is the problem.

(b) TRIAGE THE 282 — each becomes one of: a runnable check, an honestly downgraded claim, or deleted. Most work, most honest, and it is the only option that ends with a number that is both high and true. ⚠️ Counter: 282 items is weeks, and this project has watched a big manual sweep go stale before.

(c) DELETE RATHER THAN CONVERT. A check that cannot be re-run and was never observed failing may be worth removing rather than dignifying — 312 becomes maybe 60 real ones. ⚠️ Counter: a Verification also records INTENT to check, and deleting loses the list of what somebody thought mattered. ⭐ Counter-counter: that list is exactly what an honest `planned` status is for.

(d) RATCHET ONLY. Leave the 282, require an executable form on every NEW check, and report the legacy count as a baseline that may only shrink. Cheapest, and it matches the grandfathering this repo already uses twice (the intent-authority and vocabulary-reach gates). ⚠️ Counter: it leaves 311-passing on the record indefinitely, which is the reading that drew the criticism.

🛑 AND A DISTINCTION THAT MUST NOT BE COLLAPSED. `dec:non-goal-reflow2-does-not-judge-whether-a-check-is-meaningful` (ACCEPTED) says a passing Verification is a claim reflow2 RECORDS, never one it VALIDATES. Everything above is about THIS REPOSITORY'S OWN STANDARD, not about reflow2 judging a user's checks. Whether the product should also offer this as a report to consumers is a separate question and should not be settled by answering this one.
properties.name: OPEN — what must a check BE before the design counts it? 282 of 312 cannot be re-run, and until this is answered "288 capabilities have CI checks" is 288 claims
properties.rationale: Recorded first among the four because the other three are unanswerable without it: you cannot put CI checks on 288 capabilities until "a check" means something a machine can run, and you cannot measure progress toward it while the counter treats a claim and a run as the same event.
